A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIF and LossDiff-IRM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated by the conference reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original influence-function analyses, DPO and SLiC alignment experiments, component ablations, and validation-noise and validation-data experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Arena-Hard evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, threshold-sensitivity results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The TIF criterion, LossDiff and IRM scores, intersection-based selection rule, and warm-up, auxiliary-model training and retraining procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. Additional threshold documentation and analyses do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Arena-Hard, containing 500 challenging prompts, to the existing open-ended generation evaluations. UltraChat, UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval and Vicuna-Bench remain, as do the appendix experiments using OASST and GoldenHH. This extends coverage within the existing task family.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates CurriDPO-GPT4, CurriDPO-Reward Model, MAP and RS-DPO against LossDiff-IRM on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B-Base with DPO. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison methods beyond v1’s retained filtering, random-selection, full-data and exact-TIF comparisons; CurriDPO was previously only discussed.

E3.justification: New experiments sweep symmetric percentile cutoffs over 0, 10, 20 and 30 and compare processing time with RS-DPO using eight responses per prompt on one H100 GPU. Existing training budgets, data splits, generation settings, judges and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds threshold-sensitivity analyses for two 8B models, score-distribution diagnostics, and runtime comparisons with RS-DPO (Figures 6, 14–15 and Table 14). Component ablations also extend to Arena-Hard. The earlier noise, overlapping-subset, selected-versus-dropped and validation-source analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix D.3 retains the same answer-order swapping and averaged pairwise evaluation. The new theoretical variance calculation is not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original three-benchmark Table 3 scores remain identical, while v2 adds Arena-Hard scores and new baseline, sensitivity and timing results. For example, new Table 4 reports Qwen AlpacaEval WinRate of 74.07 for RS-DPO versus 71.52 for LossDiff-IRM. Aggregate improvement summaries also change alongside the expanded benchmark coverage.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 introduces a clean/noisy validation-gradient model, independence and isotropic-noise assumptions, and variance/correlation reasoning intended to justify medium-IF selection. Appendix A.1 also corrects the expected-reward sign in Equation 11. The existing LossDiff lemma and SLiC derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: model-dependent preference-data quality, the usefulness of medium-IF pairs, an efficient LossDiff-IRM approximation, and improved alignment using less data. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explains threshold sensitivity as initially removing poor data and subsequently excluding useful pairs. It also interprets score distributions as supporting adequate selection overlap, discusses why MAP and RS-DPO are strong model-dependent competitors, and explains their computational tradeoffs. Earlier interpretations and qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public-code URL and reproducibility statement, Arena-Hard access information, and the RS-DPO timing configuration. Appendix E.6 newly states default threshold choices, although duplicated bound names make that statement imprecise. The original training-hyperparameter table is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including MAP, RS-DPO and Arena-Hard, plus several background works. Its comparison discussion acknowledges that MAP and RS-DPO partly incorporate the model’s perspective. This qualifies the positioning while preserving the existing related-work structure and central motivation.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the Sections 1–6 and appendices A–E organization are retained. v2 adds experimental discussion, appendix subsections, acknowledgments, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements, and updates author/header information. It does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes typography, margins, headers and figure/table placement throughout. Table 3 gains Arena-Hard columns, component-ablation figures expand from six to eight panels, and new comparison tables, threshold plots and distribution plots are added. Existing appendix prompts and analyses are redistributed rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The added direct comparisons, Arena-Hard evaluation and threshold tests improve the empirical support, while the code link improves access information. These gains are tempered by the incomplete argument for middle-ranked superiority in new Appendix B.3 and inaccurate summary reporting: the revised Qwen average gain is 15.14%, whereas Table 3 implies approximately 11.22%.
